A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AutoGPS framework. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original Geometry3K and PGPS9K evaluations, a 100-problem human reasoning evaluation, formalization measurements and component ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds MathVista (GPS), GeoQA, answer-reliability, timing and feedback-refinement evaluations in Appendix B.

M1.justification: The MPF pipeline, validation-feedback loop, deductive/algebraic reasoning operations and minimal-solution procedure are retained. The new refinement ablation tests an existing mechanism; the added AlphaGeometry discussion changes attribution and explanation, not the algorithm.

E1.justification: v2 adds actual evaluation on MathVista's GPS subset and GeoQA (Appendix B, Tables 2–3), substantially extending the original Geometry3K/PGPS9K coverage. GeoQA also appears in the feedback-refinement comparison. These datasets were only cited, not evaluated, in v1.

E2.justification: The main Table 1 comparator set is retained, but v2 adds HyperGNet to the existing ground-truth-formalization comparison. New benchmark comparisons include DreamPRM, Ovis2_34B, SCA-GPS and DualGeoSolver, among others. Pass@5 and Major@5 also become explicit refinement controls. HyperGNet and FGeo-HyperGNet cite the same work.

E3.justification: Appendix B introduces conditional Answer Reliability Rate scoring with model-specific valid-answer criteria, timing-distribution evaluation and a five-pass refinement-versus-sampling comparison. These substantially extend the evaluation design. The original Choice/Completion rules, Pass@3 convention, human-evaluation procedure, decoding settings and 1800-second timeout remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds answer-reliability analysis, DSR runtime distributions and a feedback-refinement ablation against independent sampling and self-consistency. It also illustrates and analyzes the previously reported single AutoGPS reasoning-evaluation failure. Existing noise examples, geometry-validation ablation and deductive/algebraic reasoning ablation are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty across replicated experiments. The original Pass@3 description remains. The new five-pass comparison changes inference budgets, while timing percentiles describe variation across problems rather than repeated-run uncertainty.

E6.justification: Main Table 1 scores remain unchanged. New results include 86.2% Choice accuracy on both added datasets, Refine@5 Completion scores of 71.2%, 73.3% and 71.9%, and ARR/timing measurements. Figure 11 implies AutoGPS–InterGPS ARR gaps reaching 12.3 percentage points, whereas the accompanying prose states a maximum of 11.8.

T1.justification: v2 introduces the mathematical definition ARR = N_correct/N_valid in Appendix B, Equation 2. The hypergraph formalism, acyclicity and minimality conditions, shortest-path complexity assertion, algebraic derivations and appendix formal-language grammar remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central contribution: multimodal formalization coupled with symbolic reasoning for concise, reliable and interpretable geometry solutions. The headline state-of-the-art claims, 99% logical-coherence result and introductory performance margins are unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 expands the failure discussion with proposed labeling and training-corpus explanations, distinguishes faithful formalization from internal consistency, and notes that conditioning human evaluation on correct answers favors simpler MLLM problems. It also interprets the new reliability and efficiency results. The three formal limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v1's project-homepage link is removed. A new reproducibility statement says code and data accompany the supplementary materials and promises a public codebase; this is stated access information, not independently verified availability. Existing hardware, hyperparameters, timeout and prompt templates are retained.

R1.justification: New Section 2.3 substantially broadens positioning through neural-symbolic theorem proving, verified data generation and tool-using agents. v2 adds works such as NeSyGeo, LeanDojo and rStar2-Agent, explicitly credits InterGPS and AlphaGeometry as methodological influences, and distinguishes AutoGPS's general algebraic solving from AlphaGeometry.

P1.justification: Most core prose and the main narrative remain intact. v2 adds a related-work subsection and closing statements, expands Appendix B, moves the symbolic-solver comparison there, and reletters the appendices. Citation style, headings and selected explanations are revised without extensive rewriting of the retained text.

P2.justification: v2 adds three tables for benchmark and refinement comparisons and three figures covering ARR, the failure case and four timing distributions. The original symbolic-comparison table is relocated and expanded. Conference formatting, float placement and several captions change, while existing worked examples and hypergraph illustrations are retained under new numbering.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, v2 provides useful direct evidence about feedback refinement and computational cost, broadens benchmark validation, and clarifies formalization failures and human-evaluation selection effects. These strengthen the paper, but the added benchmark and refinement experiments have sparse setup documentation, and the ARR discussion contains a numerical inconsistency. The net improvement is therefore limited.
